description.narrative: The objective of the Emergency Tubercolosis Project is to improve the quality and expand the coverage and utilization of health services to control the spread of tuberculosis in targeted areas of Papua New Guinea by strengthening programmatic management of tuberculosis. There are three components to the project, the first component being early detection of active tuberculosis patients. The IDA credit will finance the implementation of ACF strategies, which have been developed for Western Province and are also included in the NCD TB plan. Financing will be provided for procurement of diagnostic medical devices and consumables, technical assistance, and other eligible expenditures deemed necessary for the early detection of active TB patients. The second component is the effective treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant tuberculosis patients. The project will support the effective treatment of both DS and DR TB patients, including the new short regimen for DR TB patients, through three subcomponents: improving clinical management of DS TB and DR TB; strengthening the directly observed treatment implementation and reduce the loss of follow up of patients in the BMUs; and supporting social mobilization in targeted areas. Finally, the third component is the strengthen the recipient's systems for managing its health services delivery and tuberculosis response.

To Improve the quality and expand the coverage and utilization of health services to control the spread of tuberculosis in targeted areas of Papua New Guinea by strengthening programmatic management of tuberculosis.

condition.narrative: No later than three months after the effective date, the Recipient shall prepare and adopt a Project Operational Manual, acceptableto the Association, giving details of guidelines and procedures agreed with the Association for implementation, supervision, andmonitoring and evaluation of the Project.

No later than three months after the effectiveness date, the Recipient shall establish and maintain a Project management unitwithin the National Health Services Standards Section of NDOH which shall be maintained with terms of reference, composition andresources at all times satisfactory to the Association.

No later than two months after the effective date and November 30 of each year for every subsequent year during the implementationof the Project (or such later date as the Association may agree), the Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association forno-objection, an Annual Work Plan and Budget in accordance with the terms of the Financing Agreement.

title.narrative: Number of BMUs using e-health information system for TB case and laboratory management in targeted geographic areas (NCD & Western Province)

comment.narrative: In NCD, all 14 BMUs have integrated an e- TB Module. However, within the Western Province, only Balimo BMU is currently using the e-TB Modules. Up to 15 Sites for both Province. Remote Sensing has advised the NTP, that the implementation of e-TB roll out in the Western Province is projected to be completed by 2024. For Western Province, NTP with the support from DFAT, they are planning to implement e-TB roll out in 2024. Now they are only supporting Balimo BMU. This year 2024, NTP will support and install e-TB modules for the other 5 BMUs including Daru Hospital, Tabubil Hospital, Kiunga Hospital, and Mabaduan Health Center).

title.narrative: Number of BMUs where all clinical staff have been trained/retrained on TB and DR TB (NCD and Western Province)

comment.narrative: In NCD, all the 14 BMU with their officers in total up to 25 were trained this year 2023. for both DSTB and DRTB. STC officers attached with MSF in the TB BMU were also trained. For Western Province, 6 trained BMU officers are assigned to each of the 6 reporting BMUs. In collaboration with WHO, 26 clinical staff from different health facilities of Western Province were trained on DR-TB management in 2023. (Daru Hospital, Tabubil Hospital, Kiunga Hospital, Balimo Hospital, Mabaduan Health Center). There is ongoing training and mentorship by the NTP and partners (Burnet/World Vision /NTP/World Bank and other partners) Hence, the Project end of project Target was achieved, and it went beyond the expected target.

comment.narrative: The PC 3 lab at CPHL, has not been functional since January 2021. Samples of RR/MDR-TB patients have been sent to supranational lab in Australia (QMRL) for culture and DST. Culture results from QMRL are not available in 2022 to-date. To be reported in the next reporting period once the PC 3 lab is fixed. The PC3 Lab roofing in NCD is fixed, but the Air Conditioning system must be replaced as it is found to be non-functional. The CPHL TB laboratory head is mobilizing resources to procure the air-conditioning system and make a replacement. Once the air conditioning is fixed, the PC3 lab should be up and running- estimated in June 2024. Note: Q3 and Q4 2023, (July to December) data in NCD are not updated by Central Public Health Laboratory (CPHL).

title.narrative: Number of people receiving tuberculosis treatment in accordance with the national guidelines (NCD)
Number of BMUs with functioning TB Smear microscopy (NCD)

comment.narrative: As of Q4, 2023, 6 out of the 14 BMUs within NCD have operational TB smear microscopy services. These functional BMUs include CPHL, Six Mile Clinic, Gerehu General Hospital, Lawes Road Urban Clinic, Tokarar Clinic, and Nine Mile Clinic. Unfortunately, Badilli lab remains closed due to non-functional air conditioning. Moving forward from Quarter 4 2023 to March 2024, the NCD PHA has set the goal of maintaining 7 BMUs with operational TB smear microscopy services. This count comprises the 6 BMUs that were operational, along with the excluding of the Badili lab. The decision to limit services to these 7 BMUs stems from the fact that the remaining seven facilities within NCD do not encounter a sufficient volume of TB cases to justify the establishment of microscopy services.

title.narrative: Timely delivery of annual report compiled by NTP

comment.narrative: 2022 NTP Annual TB Report is complete and available. 2023 report will be available in 2024. 2023 Annual Report for TB is completed for Review by SEM. In terms of 2023 NTP BMU reports, 58% reports were timely, 22% BMUs submitted late, and 20% didn't submit their reports) Timely Reporting is a continuous issue faced in the country by NTP, almost 40% are reported late submission which affect our quarterly report but working closely with the PHAs to fix this gap.

title.narrative: Citizens and/or communities involved in planning/ implementation/ evaluation of development programs

comment.narrative: Continuous engagement with individual citizens and communities remains an active effort. Collaborative efforts involve community-based organizations aligned with TB program to implement TB Services along with developmental partners, NGOs, and stakeholders, fostering a combined approach toward TB eradication. Evaluation of the BMU performance is done through quarterly review meetings, involving NCD PHA, NTP, WHO, World Vision, and other partners.

The forthcoming high-level meeting involving the Prime Minister and Health Minister is planned but dates are not confirmed as yet. title.narrative: Project-supported organization(s) publishing reports containing information on feedback received from citizens and/or communities and if/how this feedback has been used

comment.narrative: The wide TB alliance and program partners, including valued Partners like World Vision and MSF actively contribute by sharing feedback and reports with the NTP. These inputs undergo thorough review under the joint guidance of partners and the program manager, ensuring a collaborative and informed approach. For the SSI Project in NCD, community feedback for the project is received on daily basis for improvement and progress of the project on a daily/weekly basis. Implementation Completion Report will be done and shared in at the end of March 2024 so the reports and the publication can be done accordingly.

title.narrative: Population-based screening in Daru is complete

comment.narrative: There is still population – based screening going on in Daru which is an ongoing active case finding in the community with the support from Burnet Institute and World Vision Australia. Daru population-based screening for active TB was completed in 2019 and results were disseminated through stakeholder meetings. WHO initiated a process to publish an article on BMC public health with the title “Yield of systematic screening for active TB among the population in Daru, South Fly District, Western Province, Papua New Guinea.” The article has been accepted for publication and payment for the publication is in process. Now TB SWEEP Project by Burnet Institute is doing ongoing and mass screening at Daru Island, capturing a lot of patients and community. 34 New TB cases have been identified and reported for 5 months and are still on going. The screening is similar to the systematic screening in NCD.

title.narrative: Population-based screening in NCD is ongoing

comment.narrative: The Emergency TB Project, TB Systematic Screening Intervention (SSI) is currently engaged in active case finding in NCD within the TB hotspot communities. This screening initiative have detected a substantial number of TB cases. This population screening program is scheduled to span a duration of five months, commencing from October 2023 and concluding on June 15, 2024, with a primary focus on early screening, prompt diagnosis, and timely intervention. The main objective of this endeavor is to ease the spread of TB within the community by facilitating early detection and subsequent treatment.
